title: Choose the visual world for brickbot.ro (bolder hand)
question: Bolder hand, centred on the current season and the team's energy; conversion stays quiet. The deal put Charged Basin first. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Charged Basin
options.lineage: suminagashi ink basin, recast as electric charge
options.thesis: The page is a live field of yellow charge on black: your pointer drags currents through it, and the DECODE season sits still in the margin.
materials: yellow charge dye thinning to grey
options.viewport: The whole screen is the basin: a fresh surge of yellow charge is the brightest thing, and team photos surface through the currents. A still margin holds 'FTC #15996, division finalists at the 2026 FIRST Championship' and one quiet 'Partner with us'.
options.risk: Abstract: it can read as an art piece rather than a robotics team, and a glowing field on black is near the neon look you ruled out.

raised.raise: Things register in order: photo, then result, then the yellow last, so the page builds brick by brick.
Every event in the season is ruled by one strict label grid: event, date, result, award.
Every photo carries a small ticket of origin: event, city, date.

options.label: Race Livery
options.lineage: printed vinyl race wraps with sponsor strips along the sill
options.thesis: The site is wrapped like a race livery: the team's photos printed huge across panels and seams, the 15996 roundel, and sponsor strips along the sill.
options.viewport: One wrapped body across the screen: the Worlds 2026 celebration photo scaled so large it breaks across two panels with a seam through it, the 15996 roundel on the 'door', the result in the livery type, and the 2025–26 sponsors as a logo strip along the bottom sill.
options.case: Beats the leader on both counts: sponsors see exactly where their logo goes (logo on the robot is a real tier benefit), and it is about performance, speed and this season.
options.risk: Motorsport graphics can tip into esports branding if the seams and strips get decorative instead of structural.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.thesis: This season's numbers glow as stacked yellow digits in glass tubes, and each result arrives as a visible count.
options.viewport: A bank of tubes counts up to 15996, then the season ticks into place: the Worlds division finals, Design Award 2nd place, the national final. Labels are engraved below each bank.
options.case: Strong on performance: the results become the interface. Weaker on people and on the impact on them.
options.risk: Numbers without faces, and a glow that sits close to neon.

options.label: Shell-Ground Print
options.thesis: The season printed block by block on a glittering ground.
options.viewport: A team photo built up colour block by colour block.
options.case: Declined: folk-print craft says little about robots or competing.

options.label: Box Wall
options.thesis: Results as boxes pulled from a stacked wall.
options.viewport: A wall of labelled boxes, one per event.
options.case: Declined: a retail archive, and the board colour fights the brand.
options.kept: A strict label grid on every card.

options.label: Shadow Bazaar
options.thesis: Moments traded like shadows at night stalls.
options.case: Declined: dreamy, the opposite of electric, and it hides the robot.
options.kept: Every item carries a ticket of origin.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark robotics-team site with a yellow accent, executed with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Team photo hero with a headline and two buttons, then the season, posts and sponsors.
canonCard.risk: Close to the removed first attempt; it reads like every other team's site.
